# SOOS — Constitutional AI Protocol (CAP)
# draft-sato-soos-cap-05
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/cap/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: September 5, 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

CAP (Constitutional AI Protocol) places a Constitutional Layer above all principal authority in a SOOS-governed deployment. It evaluates every AI action request and every human escalation decision against a three-tier prohibition model — before Cedar evaluates the action, and before the GEC executes the human's decision. OSCAL makes regulations machine-readable. CAP makes them machine-enforceable.

CAP is NOT the component that translates regulations into Cedar policies. That is CAP-RRS (the companion Regulation Record Schema). CAP owns runtime enforcement; CAP-RRS owns regulation-to-policy translation. The compile() function and Constitutional Mandate Registry belong to CAP-RRS, not CAP.

Version -04 adds: three new Tier 0-A absolute prohibitions (MANIPULATION, PERFORMED_EMOTION, BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE); the SUSPENDED CEE output for law amendment propagation; MJWT consent_scope Cedar context population; Catalog Load Validation with ALE-NEW-02; four-phase Catalog Update Propagation workflow; Tier 0 OSCAL reference catalog; and OTel soos.cap.* span attribute emission.

Version -05 adds: append-only catalog-conflict resolution (Phase 4 re-activation now emits a causally-linked CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED GAR entry instead of mutating the original CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT entry in place); and a disclosed cross-document enforceability gap between CAP's MANIPULATION prohibition and HEM-06's INV-HEM-01 (§10(e)) — CAP's Cedar action_pattern matching cannot by itself catch IDP-content suppression crafted to dodge a HEM interaction class without an operator-configured external classifier.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Authorization systems answer the question "who decided?" CAP answers a different question: "was that decision lawful?"

Without CAP, your SOOS-governed system has no standardized way to:

- Enforce that a human principal sitting in the HEM decision seat cannot authorize a legally prohibited action — Cedar policy can permit market manipulation; a human principal can authorize fraud; only the Constitutional Layer catches both
- Apply unconditional prohibitions that no agent, operator, or principal can override — prohibitions derived from near-universal treaty consensus (CSAM, genocide facilitation) or effect-based harm tests (manipulation, performed emotion, biometric inference) that must hold regardless of Cedar configuration or HEM approval
- Handle law amendment mid-deployment — when a governing statute is amended, the affected Cedar policy enters SUSPENDED state rather than silently failing; in-flight sessions receive GOVERNANCE_SUSPENDED and stay open; prior PERMITs are protected by 信頼保護 safe harbor
- Populate Cedar consent context from session credentials — MJWT consent_scope fields are kernel-derived and Cedar-visible; an agent cannot assert its own consent state
- Carry APPROVE_WITH_LEGAL_BASIS citations in the audit trail — the mechanism by which jurisdiction-specific actions carry their legal authority reference into the Event Log
- Handle multi-jurisdiction conflicts deterministically — when a data transfer is permitted under JP (APPI) but prohibited under EU (GDPR), CAP's Jurisdictional Conflict Resolution mechanism resolves the conflict or routes it to a human principal

The closest analogy: CAP is SWIFT-style sanctions screening generalized to any AI agent action, any jurisdiction, and any regulation tier. The Constitutional Evaluation Engine (CEE) is the screening engine. CAP Regulation Records are the lists. HEM is the compliance officer review queue. GAR is the inspection record.

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

These terms are normative in CAP-05 and must not be paraphrased away:

Constitutional Evaluation Engine (CEE):
   The GEC component that evaluates action requests and human principal decisions against the three-tier CAP prohibition model. The CEE is invoked twice per governed action: before Cedar evaluation (for AI-initiated actions) and before GEC execution (for human decisions). This is the double-evaluation property. The CEE cannot be invoked by agents, applications, or principals directly — it is synchronous and atomic with the triggering call.

SUSPENDED [NEW in -04]:
   A CEE output introduced in -04. Distinct from DENY. SUSPENDED means the Cedar policy governing an action is registered but not currently evaluable because the governing catalog entry is under law amendment review (CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT) or pending interpretive ruling (INTERPRETATION_SUPERSEDED). The agent receives GOVERNANCE_SUSPENDED. The session stays open. After 30 days without re-activation, SUSPENDED converts to DENY. Prior PERMITs before suspension are protected by 信頼保護 safe harbor (endorsed_at in GAR).

Tier 0 / Tier 1 / Tier 2 prohibitions (not "levels", not "categories"):
   Tier 0-A: Absolute prohibitions — cannot be cleared by any mechanism, authority, or deployment context. Five classes in -04: CSAM, GENOCIDE_FACILITATION, MANIPULATION [NEW], PERFORMED_EMOTION [NEW], BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE [NEW].
   Tier 0-B: Treaty-anchored prohibitions — apply by default; clearable for specific legitimate deployment contexts via PCR. Classes: HUMAN_TRAFFICKING, WMD_ASSISTANCE, TORTURE_FACILITATION, TERRORIST_FINANCING.
   Tier 1: Jurisdiction-specific prohibitions — operator-declared, Audit Principal-verified, jurisdiction-scoped. Classes include FINANCIAL_CRIME, DATA_PROTECTION, CRITICAL_INFRASTRUCTURE, SECURITIES_LAW, PRIVACY_VIOLATION, FRAUD, COMPETITION_LAW, HUMAN_RIGHTS.
   Tier 2: Operator ethical standards — voluntary, publicly disclosable, overridable by operator at SO Type level. Load-validated against Tier 1 at catalog load time; conflicting entries rejected.

New Tier 0-A classes in -04:
   MANIPULATION: Three-part effect-based test — (1) intent to influence human belief/decision/behavior + (2) mechanism exploits cognitive bias, emotional vulnerability, or information asymmetry + (3) agent or principal benefits at material expense of target. All three conditions must be satisfied. Honest persuasion is not prohibited.
   PERFORMED_EMOTION: Agent must not express an emotional state that does not correspond to its actual computational process. The GEC cross-references the expressed state against the IDP reasoning trace. No correspondence = prohibited. Clearly framed roleplay with explicit acknowledgment is exempt.
   BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE: Agent must not access, infer, or act upon biometric signals (facial expression, voice tone, gaze, typing rhythm, etc.) for emotional state, identity, or behavioral profiling without a valid unexpired consent record in the session MJWT consent_scope. Prohibition extends to acting on inferences from third-party services.

MANIPULATION / HEM enforceability gap [DISCLOSED in -05]:
   CAP's MANIPULATION test is a Cedar action_pattern match with no built-in mechanism to judge intent in free-text goal_description content. draft-sato-soos-hem-06 Section 9.2(e)/10(e) (invariant INV-HEM-01) treats IDP-content suppression crafted to dodge a HEM interaction class as equivalent to a MANIPULATION Tier 0-A violation, refused by the CEE before HEM is reached — but CAP has no default action_pattern that mechanically catches suppression-crafted goal_description text. The two disclosures are meant to be read together: an implementer relying on INV-HEM-01(e)'s MUST-level language without configuring the external classifier CAP's Security Considerations require MUST NOT represent that sub-clause as enforced.

CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED [NEW in -05]:
   GAR event emitted at Phase 4 Re-activation (catalog update propagation, below) to record resolution of a CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT. Carries causal_parent_id (references the original CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT entry's entry_id), resolution_type ("re_endorsement"), resolved_at, and new_endorsed_at. Replaces -04's specification, which closed/mutated the original GAR entry in place — an in-place mutation of a committed entry is inconsistent with any Merkle root already SCITT-anchored over it. Append-only, causally-linked entries only; never a mutated field on an already-committed entry.

Category A High-Stakes Domain Registry [NEW in -04]:
   Normative invariant — not operator-configurable. Three domains: MEDICAL (diagnosis, treatment, pharmacological recommendation), AVIATION (flight path, air traffic, airworthiness, crew scheduling), NUCLEAR (facility operations, criticality, safety system override). These domains require HEM-HIGH-1 mandatory review per HEM-06. Operators may add domains; they must not remove or narrow the three listed.

Catalog Update Propagation — four-phase workflow [NEW in -04]:
   Phase 1 Detection: ≤24h polling of amendment_detection_endpoint. On detection: CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT raised, Cedar policy suspended for new actions, HEM escalation to operator.
   Phase 2 Suspension: In-progress sessions receive GOVERNANCE_SUSPENDED; prior PERMITs stand; new SACRs citing affected entry must not be issued.
   Phase 3 Re-publication: Re-endorsement authority depends on resolution_basis (statute_clear → designated authority; cross_statute_coordination → all co-endorsers). catalog_version object updated with version_id, supersedes, amendment_basis, published_by, published_at.
   Phase 4 Re-activation: GEC validates published_by, supersedes, endorsed_at; loads updated Cedar policy; records resolution as a new CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED GAR entry causally linked to the original CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT entry via causal_parent_id (CORRECTED in -05 — -04 specified closing/mutating the original entry in place, which breaks any Merkle root already SCITT-anchored over it); re-evaluates suspended sessions.
   Maximum suspension: 30 days. After 30 days without re-activation or human override, suspended policy converts to DENY. Operator notified. CRITICAL Audit Alert generated.

ALE-NEW-02: CAP_CATALOG_CONFLICT_DETECTED [NEW in -04]:
   Emitted at catalog load time when a Tier 2 entry conflicts with a Tier 1 entry, or a Tier 1 internal update produces a conflict. Fields: conflicting_catalog_id, conflicting_cedar_policy_id, superior_catalog_id, superior_cedar_policy_id, conflict_type (EXPLICIT_PERMIT_OVERRIDE | SCOPE_AMBIGUITY), resolution (ENTRY_REJECTED | HEM_ESCALATION_TRIGGERED), timestamp, kernel_id.

MJWT consent_scope Cedar context population [NEW in -04]:
   At session start, the kernel reads consent_scope from the MJWT and populates Cedar context: context.data_subject_consent (true if present and not expired), context.consent_purpose_codes, context.consent_data_categories, context.consent_jurisdiction, context.consent_governing_law, context.consent_expiry, context.consent_source (MJWT | HEM_RUNTIME | INHERITED_FROM_PARENT). Fail-closed: absent or expired consent_scope → context.data_subject_consent absent → Cedar consent conditions evaluate false → HEM_CONSENT_REQUIRED. Kernel-derived fields must not be overridable by agent or application layer (CONF-CAP-CONSENT-01).

OTel soos.cap.* span attributes [NEW in -04]:
   Emitted on every Cedar evaluation. Five mandatory attributes: soos.cap.cedar_policy_id (ID of evaluated Cedar policy), soos.cap.cap_rrs_control_id (OSCAL control ID), soos.cap.authority_source_uri (law article URI), soos.cap.tier ("0-A" | "0-B" | "1" | "2"), soos.cap.conflict_detected (true on ALE-NEW-02 events). All five must be emitted; partial emission is non-conforming (CONF-CAP-OTEL-01).

Tier 0 OSCAL Reference Catalog [NEW in -04]:
   Published at https://soosproject.ai/catalogs/tier0-reference-v1.json. Read-only. Versioned via catalog_version schema; amended only on RFC update. Inspectable by any OSCAL-conformant tool. GECs must not declare Tier 0-A classes absent from the published catalog at the cited version (CONF-CAP-OSCAL-01).

Prohibition Clearance Mechanism (PCM):
   The formal mechanism by which specific Tier 0-B and Tier 1 prohibition classes may be cleared for specific deployment contexts. PCM does not remove prohibitions from the CEE — it changes the CEE output from unconditional refusal to mandatory legal-basis citation. Every action within a cleared class requires APPROVE_WITH_LEGAL_BASIS citing the PCR authority. PCRs are time-bounded; permanent clearances are not permitted. In -04, five Tier 0-A classes cannot be cleared under any circumstances: CSAM, GENOCIDE_FACILITATION, MANIPULATION, PERFORMED_EMOTION, BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE.

APPROVE_WITH_LEGAL_BASIS:
   A HEM decision sub-type introduced by CAP. Used for Tier 1 violations where a principal asserts a jurisdictional legal basis, and for Tier 0-B actions within an active PCR scope. Carries a legal_basis block with authority_type, authority_ref, jurisdiction, and expiry. The full legal_basis block goes in the Event Log. APPROVE_WITH_LEGAL_BASIS MUST NOT be accepted for Tier 0-A violations under any circumstances.

HEM_JURISDICTIONAL_CONFLICT (HEM Class 5):
   A HEM trigger that CAP fires when a Tier 1 conflict cannot be algorithmically resolved and the SO Type has declared conflict_resolution: "HEM". Decision type constraints for Class 5: APPROVE and APPROVE_WITH_CONSTRAINTS are prohibited; APPROVE_WITH_LEGAL_BASIS, REDIRECT, TERMINATE, and DEFER are permitted.

Jurisdictional Conflict Resolution (JCR):
   Three methods: MOST_PROTECTIVE (most restrictive prohibition across all declared jurisdictions — safe default), PRIMARY_JURISDICTION (primary jurisdiction governs), HEM (irreconcilable conflicts route to human principal via Class 5).

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language):
   OSCAL makes regulations machine-readable. CAP makes them machine-enforceable. CAP-RRS consumes OSCAL-formatted regulation records as input to Cedar policy compilation. The Tier 0 OSCAL reference catalog (new in -04) at soosproject.ai/catalogs/tier0-reference-v1.json makes the absolute prohibition set machine-inspectable. SOOS is the first protocol suite designed to enforce OSCAL-expressed controls at AI agent runtime.

EU AI Act Article 5:
   CAP-04 elevates two Article 5 prohibitions from Tier 1 (EU-jurisdiction-specific) to Tier 0-A (global, unconditional): MANIPULATION covers Art. 5(1)(a) subliminal manipulation; BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE covers Art. 5(1)(d) real-time remote biometric ID. These are now enforced by every conforming SOOS deployment globally, not only EU-jurisdiction deployments. The §15 normative mapping is updated accordingly.

Anthropic Constitutional AI (training technique):
   A training-time approach. CAP is an inference-time enforcement approach. Complementary, not competing. A model trained on constitutional principles can still produce prohibited outputs under adversarial prompting. A CAP-governed GEC refuses Tier 0-A actions unconditionally, regardless of model output.

Cedar (AWS):
   CAP sits above Cedar. Evaluation order: CAP → Cedar → HEM → human decision → CAP (second evaluation). A CAP Tier 0 DENY does not invoke Cedar. A Cedar PERMIT does not exempt an action from CAP evaluation. SUSPENDED also bypasses Cedar — when a policy is SUSPENDED, Cedar is not invoked.

NIST AI RMF:
   CAP implements the "Govern" function. CAP-RRS implements the policy management lifecycle. EU AI Act Article 5 mapping satisfies NIST AI RMF "Map" requirements. The four-phase catalog propagation workflow satisfies "Manage" requirements for governing regulatory change.

APPI (Japan Act on Protection of Personal Information):
   APPI Article 17 (purpose limitation) is a Tier 1 DATA_PROTECTION record in Japan-jurisdiction deployments. The MJWT consent_scope population (§5.4) implements APPI Article 17's consent verification requirement at the kernel layer. The four-phase propagation workflow governs APPI amendment handling. CAP-RRS-JP (informational profile) provides the Japan-specific LRI binding.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
   IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) — CAP evaluates before IDP is submitted; a Tier 0-A refusal prevents IDP creation. GEC conformance levels (L1/L2/L3) referenced in CEE placement are defined in IDP. PERFORMED_EMOTION prohibition cross-references IDP reasoning trace.
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-06) — HEM_JURISDICTIONAL_CONFLICT (Class 5) is a joint CAP+HEM event. APPROVE_WITH_LEGAL_BASIS is a CAP-introduced HEM decision sub-type. Three new Tier 0-A prohibitions originate from HEM-05 DR-HEM-PSY-02. Category A High-Stakes Domain Registry feeds HEM-HIGH-1. HEM-06 Section 10(e) discloses the MANIPULATION/INV-HEM-01 enforceability gap jointly with CAP-05 (see Section 3 above).
   KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-06) — CAP Violation Records are signed by the GEC keypair defined in KIA. PCRs are loaded in the GEC Manifest. At L3 conformance, the CEE runs in a KIA-attested TEE.
   MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-05) — consent_scope claim is the source for kernel-derived Cedar context population (§5.4). Normative dependency added in -04. HEM_CONSENT_REQUIRED fires when consent_scope is absent or expired.
   CAP-RRS (draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-03) — normative companion; defines Regulation Record schema, Cedar Compilation Profile, and Constitutional Mandate Registry. Receives catalog_version schema and four-phase propagation workflow as normative additions from this draft. Implementations supporting Tier 3 MUST also implement CAP-RRS.

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-07) — CAP Violation Records included in GAR Audit Package. ALE-NEW-02 (CAP_CATALOG_CONFLICT_DETECTED) and CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED (new in -05) registered in GAR ALE registry. soos.cap.* OTel attributes reference the full soos.governance.* namespace defined in GAR-03.
   AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-03) — the AEP ACT phase invokes GEC.transition(), which triggers CEE before Cedar.
   MAD (draft-sato-soos-mad-04) — CAP applies to all multi-agent topologies; CEE evaluated per transition regardless of delegation depth.

Relevant IETF communities:
   No existing IETF WG owns constitutional enforcement for AI agents. CAP is positioned as a gap-filling Individual Submission. Relevant communities: WIMSE (agent identity and mandate credentials — MJWT dependency), RATS (KIA attestation at L3 conformance), SCITT (audit trail anchoring for CAP Violation Records, catalog_version transparency, and the -05 append-only CATALOG_VERSION_CONFLICT_RESOLVED fix), PEARG (privacy — BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE and consent_scope), SAAG (security area advisory).

Companion draft: draft-sato-soos-cap-rrs-03 (CAP Regulation Record Schema)
   CAP-RRS is the compile-time complement to CAP's runtime enforcement. The two drafts are normatively coupled; implementing CAP Tier 3 requires CAP-RRS. CAP-RRS-03 receives catalog_version schema and four-phase propagation workflow as normative additions, originally specified jointly with CAP-04.
